lesson_title: Photo Day: Year-End, the Gauges and the Guards
hook_text: Once a year, every business takes ONE photo — and banks, tax offices and owners all stake money on it being honest.
clip_script: Year-end is photo day: one picture of the business, taken at midnight on the last day, that outsiders will trust. But before any photo, you tidy the room — and that is all the adjustments are. The bakkie in the yard is not worth what it cost three years ago; the books must admit the wearing — that is depreciation, twelve thousand two hundred rand of honesty, no cash moving, only truth arriving. The February phone calls billed in March belong to THIS year's picture — pull them in. The insurance paid ahead for next year does not belong — push it out. The tenant's rent, earned but not yet received — pull it in. Four movements, one principle: the photo must show what this year truly used and truly earned, not what the bank account happened to witness. Skip the tidying and the photo flatters or slanders — richer than it is, cheaper than it was. The neat photo is not for the photographer. It is for everyone who must trust the picture.
visual_style: A shop interior freezing into a photograph at midnight: items glowing as they are pulled into frame (owed bills, earned rent) or pushed out (next year's insurance), a bakkie visibly weathering, ending on a framed balanced statement.
mood: Honest and grounded — accounting as truth-telling before an audience.
pacing: Four tidying beats in rhythm, a held still on the finished photo, quiet close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and tidy the year before the photo.
